transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-31 15:00 UTC
Length: 56 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Tran (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Rajesh Patel (StellarBridge Head of Partnerships), Emily Chong (VP Sales), Liam O'Connor (Cloud Architect), Sofia Martins (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Agree next steps for pilot + benchmarks
- Identify legal/data residency gating items
- Work through close-plan milestones and POC scope

00:00 Alicia Tran: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — good to see the StellarBridge crew. we set aside about an hour to run through the cross-border co-sell risks, close plan and pilot scope. Marco, can you lead the perf piece when we get there?
00:18 Rajesh Patel: Yep thanks Alicia, appreciate it. quick note we have a couple of pilot accounts that are EU-first and one APAC retail partner so regs matter.
00:32 Emily Chong: Hi team — big priority for us is having a partner-reseller agreement that doesn't blow up margin and clearly who owns enterprise support. also need to know about data residency, if tokens/logs leave region.
00:50 Marco Ruiz: cool, i'll walk through the technical constraints, KV cache, routing options and what Redwood Private looks like for on-prem or customer VPC. some of the terms in our docs might be off slightly in this transcript, sorry in advance.
01:05 Liam O'Connor: quick question — when you say Redwood Private, is that full air gap or a VPC with egress controls? we've got strict PCI-like controls for one account.
01:18 Marco Ruiz: right — right now Private can be deployed as customer-managed VPC or an on-prem bring-your-own infra package. for true air-gap, we have an on-prem option but that adds timeline and professional services.
01:33 Sofia Martins: legal here — can you confirm retention of logs, who holds keys, and do you offer KMS/HSM integration? also will need SOC2 and ISO docs.
01:45 Alicia Tran: yes, we can share SOC2 report and our ISO attestation, and we support KMS integrations — i'll drop the security packet in the follow up.
01:55 Rajesh Patel: perfect. on pricing — we need to ensure co-sell pricing bands allow StellarBridge to resell with a 20% margin, otherwise the economics don't work. is there flexibility on reserved capacity or partner discount tiers?
02:12 Alicia Tran: there's partner discount tiers, but pricing is linked to usage and reserved commitments. we can model a dedicated pool for pilot accounts to hit margin; we'll need to map expected token volume.
02:30 Emily Chong: the tricky part for us is variability in token usage — retail spikes are a problem. can you do burst capacity without breaking the margin math?
02:42 Marco Ruiz: yes, we have burst policies on Dedicated, but the unit economics change. we can simulate a hybrid routing: hosted for low-cost routing and fall back to dedicated when latency or throughput needs require. also caching/prefix KV caching can shave a lot off per-token costs.
03:05 Rajesh Patel: can Redwood provide estimates per-account so we can model StellarBridge resale margin?
03:12 Alicia Tran: yes we'll do a simple model — Alicia: action item to send pricing bands and a mocked cost model for three profile types (low/med/spike).

05:40 Marco Ruiz: (screen share described) i'll run through the benchmark plan: target model family is open-llama-derived variant, sequence length typical 512, we'll need to lock down quantization profile and batch sizes. for EU accounts we should consider a smaller kv cache regionally to reduce cross-region transfer.
06:05 Liam O'Connor: do you support custom kernel selection or is that handled by Redwood? on our end we mostly care about percentile P95 latency under load.
06:20 Marco Ruiz: we handle kernel selection and compilation. for Dedicated we also allow some runtime flags to tune batching per-tenant. we'll propose a benchmark config: 10k tokens/min sustained, bursts to 50k tokens/min for 10 minutes, measure p50/p95/p99.
06:40 Rajesh Patel: any gotchas with session affinity? we run long-lived chat sessions and want to avoid cold-kv cache misses.
06:54 Marco Ruiz: long-lived sessions use KV cache; for cross-region routing we can pin to region or replicate caches depending on cost. replication increases costs, so it's a tradeoff we'll quantify.

12:12 Emily Chong: back to commercial — what about lead routing and credit for closed deals? if StellarBridge brings a buyer, do we split ACV?
12:25 Alicia Tran: typical co-sell motion is partner-led with Redwood providing enablement credits and deal registration. we can discuss referral vs co-sell splits — i'll surface standard partner program terms.
12:40 Rajesh Patel: need clarity on sales credits, SLAs for Dedicated customers and who handles first-line support — partner or Redwood?
12:51 Priya Nair: CSM note: we can adopt a tiered support handoff, partner does initial triage, Redwood handles L2/L3. we include that in the partner playbook and can provision a joint runbook.
13:08 Sofia Martins: legal again — need to scope the NDA and check if there's any need for data processing addendum (DPA) for EU customers. also check cross-border transfer clauses.
13:23 Alicia Tran: understood. Alicia: action to attach our standard NDA and DPA redlines and propose minimal edits.

18:00 Marco Ruiz: some technical nuance — for the APAC retail partner you mentioned, latency to the Redwood-hosted region is about 120ms; with Dedicated in APAC we can drop that to ~40ms. question is cost vs revenue from that account.
18:20 Emily Chong: those retail accounts are sensitive to latency; a bad UX kills conversion. So if the math works, we'll prefer regional Dedicated.
18:35 Rajesh Patel: can Redwood support a split deployment where small accounts use hosted and large or latency-sensitive accounts map to regionally dedicated nodes?
18:48 Marco Ruiz: yes that's the smart routing we talked about — policy-based routing by partner/account; automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated is unavailable.

22:55 Liam O'Connor: for the benchmark we need to ensure chain-of-trust for keys; can you do per-tenant KMS and bring-your-own-key?
23:05 Marco Ruiz: per-tenant KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated for enterprise tiers. for hosted we have managed keys but we can support envelope encryption with customer KMS in some setups.
23:20 Sofia Martins: is there an audit log that shows token flows and admin access? we need to respond to infosec requests.
23:33 Alicia Tran: yes we have audit logs and can surface them, and include token-level cost/latency dashboards in Redwood Console. we'll include sample screenshots in the packet.

29:10 Rajesh Patel: risk triage — four gating items: legal (DPA/NDAs), data residency for EU accounts, regional latency for APAC retail, and pricing band clarity for reseller margin. if those four are green we can short-cycle to a pilot close.
29:33 Alicia Tran: agreed. let's set target dates: pricing packet by 2026-08-03, legal redlines by 2026-08-04, pilot account list by 2026-08-05 and benchmark kickoff week of 2026-08-10.
29:54 Rajesh Patel: that works.

35:00 Emily Chong: question — competitor behavior: we've seen Bluecrest pitch lower price but higher latency and less observability. any differentiator for Redwood that helps our sales story?
35:12 Alicia Tran: yes — our angle is predictable unit economics plus observability: token-level dashboards, per-route tracing and fallback policies. also the unified API across hosted/dedicated/private simplifies integration for partners.
35:30 Marco Ruiz: technically we also support optimization suggestions from Redwood Optimize — batching/caching suggestions and quantization recommendations tied to real prompts. that helps lower costs without regressions.

40:05 Marco Ruiz: demo note — we should run a quick simulation during the benchmark session: a 1-hour synthetic load with 256-token average queries, measure p95. that'll help decide dedicated sizing.
40:22 Alicia Tran: ok Marco will set that up. Marco: action to schedule the perf session with Liam and provide runbook.

45:15 Priya Nair: on enablement — StellarBridge sales enablement wants slide deck + one-pager and a short 30-min briefing for their AE team. Alicia: can we commit to a 30-min partner enablement session the week after the pricing packet?
45:30 Alicia Tran: yes, pencil us for 2026-08-09 for a 30-min partner enablement. we'll build a concise deck and a quick faq for their AEs.

49:00 Rajesh Patel: timeline for contract — we ideally would like to sign a pilot agreement by 2026-08-15 and start a 6-week pilot. is that realistic?
49:15 Alicia Tran: pilot by 8/15 is aggressive but feasible if legal and pricing move quick. our PS team will need a statement of work for on-prem or VPC work if Private is chosen.
49:30 Sofia Martins: note: if on-prem we need a security review and additional PS SOW; we'll budget for it but need estimates for PS hours.
49:42 Alicia Tran: Alicia: action to include estimated PS hours for on-prem or advanced Private deployment in the follow up.

53:10 Emily Chong: final recap please?
53:14 Alicia Tran: quick recap: 1) Alicia sends pricing bands, GTM one-pager, PS estimate and security packet by 8/3-8/4 window. 2) Sofia to review NDA/DPA and respond 8/4. 3) Rajesh to send pilot account list 8/5. 4) Marco to schedule perf bench with Liam week of 8/10. 5) Priya to coordinate partner enablement 8/9. Next meeting tentatively 8/12 to review legal/pricing and lock pilot if all green.
53:58 Rajesh Patel: thanks all. appreciate the clear plan.
54:10 Alicia Tran: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and the packet. bye.
54:20 (call ends)
